questions.text:
[latex]\underset{\text{I}}{\underline{\text{While trying to collect}}}[/latex] an envelope [latex]\underset{\text{II}}{\underline{\text{from under the table}}}[/latex],
[latex]\underset{\text{III}}{\underline{\text{Mr. X fell down}}}[/latex] and [latex]\underset{\text{IV}}{\underline{\text{was losing consciousness}}}[/latex].

Which one of the above underlined parts of the sentence is NOT appropriate?
questions.solution:
Falling down is a completed event, so it should be "lost consciousness". "Was losing consciousness" (continuous) does not fit.

Answer: IV

questions.text: If she _______ how to calibrate the instrument, she ________ done the experiment.
questions.solution:
Third conditional (an unreal past situation): "If + had + past participle, ... could/would have + past participle".

"If she had known how to calibrate the instrument, she could have done the experiment."

Answer: had known, could have

questions.text: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the word "coherent".
questions.solution:
Coherent = logical and well connected. Rambling = wandering, disconnected (opposite).

Answer: rambling

questions.text:
Which number does not belong in the series below?

2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, 64
questions.solution:
The terms are [latex]n^2+1[/latex]: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, 65.

The last term should be 65, not 64.

Answer: 64

questions.text:
The table below has question-wise data on the performance of students in an examination. The marks for each question are also listed. There is no negative or partial marking in the examination.

[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \textbf{Q No.} & \textbf{Marks} &\textbf{Answered}&\textbf{Answered}&\textbf{Not}\\&&\textbf{ Correctly} &\textbf{Wrongly} & \textbf{Attempted} \\\hline \text{1} & \text{2} &\text{21} &\text{17} &\text{6}\\\hline \text{2} & \text{3} &\text{15} & \text{27}& \text{2}\\\hline \text{3} & \text{2} &\text{23} & \text{18} & \text{3}\\\hline \end{array}[/latex]

What is the average of the marks obtained by the class in the examination?
questions.solution:
Marks: Q1 = 21 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 42, Q2 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 = 45, Q3 = 23 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 46 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] total 133.

Students = 21 + 17 + 6 = 44.

Average = 133 / 44 = 3.02

Answer: 3.02
